scope: Windows source development; isolated profiles, real Electron utility processes and desktop host; no configured channels or provider conversations
implementation: Native-load JavaScript doctor contracts before SDK-loader preparation, retaining the discovered plugin root and existing source/error fallbacks.
Use the existing IPv4 loopback endpoint for Main readiness/authentication, including device-token upgrade.
Make the measurement loopback-only, use per-attempt random credentials, isolate OS environment and cache, and require observed doctor-loader invocation.

measurements.cache: fresh transform cache per attempt; OS caches not flushed

acceptance.criterion: same-build alternating before/after with every sample and authenticated RPC
source/overlay authority, doctor precedence and native/fallback regression
real managed desktop start, authenticated RPC and child termination
type/build/comms/Harness results and earlier failures recorded

limitations: Three paired samples are descriptive and do not establish a statistical performance guarantee. The slow first baseline is retained.
Hot-start gains, OS-reboot cold starts, other platforms, packaged apps, and configured user/provider/channel workloads are not established.
The isolated probe disables mDNS discovery and has no configured channels; it retains normal migration and startup-sidecar behavior. Production defaults and locks are unchanged.

The original shared dependency directory could not be fully reinstalled while its Electron binary was in use. Verification used an independent frozen-lock installation with package-store reuse; runtime package dependencies were reused after manifest matching.
Earlier failed and abandoned attempts are retained in the private raw archive; they are not presented as successful runs.
